title: finding(plugin-kanban): `useColumnWidths` is exported from the package barrel with its own localStorage key and NO board reads it — a second column-width policy wired to nothing
body:
Ruled: 5810224713 · letter remove (retire useColumnWidths) · 2026-09-24T08:02Z

Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) on behalf of the objectui#8508 dev, which measured it while landing PR #8521 and correctly declined to file it: the dispatch had asked it to conserve GitHub calls after today's hour-long rate limit, and filing without a dedup search is the other forbidden shape. Handed over rather than dropped. ⛔ Not claimed.

## Measured on `origin/main`

`packages/plugin-kanban` ships **two** column-width policies. Only one of them is wired.

| | reached by | storage |
|---|---|---|
| `columnInlineStyle` (`KanbanImpl.tsx:408`) | the rendered board | none — derived per render from the board's own width |
| **`useColumnWidths`** (`useColumnWidths.ts:65`) | **nothing** | `objectui:kanban-column-widths` (`:12`) |

`useColumnWidths` is a public export — `index.tsx:129-130` exports the hook *and* `UseColumnWidthsOptions` / `UseColumnWidthsReturn` — so it is part of the package's published surface. No board component consumes it; the rendered column width comes entirely from `columnInlineStyle`, which PR #8521 has just extended to the swimlane layout as well.

It also appears in no documentation under `content/`. The dev's lit control on that instrument fired (`content/` carries plenty of kanban hits), so the zero is a real absence rather than a dead probe.

## Why it is a finding rather than a queued deletion

The hook persists per-column widths to `localStorage` under a key that only it writes. Three readings are all plausible and they lead to different work:

1. **It was the intended mechanism and was never wired** — in which case the question is whether user-resizable columns are still wanted, and `columnInlineStyle` is a container-derived *default* that a stored override should sit on top of.
2. **It was superseded by `columnInlineStyle`** and left behind — then it is a barrel export to retire under ADR-0049 (enforce-or-remove), which is a **breaking** change to the published surface and wants a `retirementTombstone()` rather than a delete.
3. **It is consumed downstream, outside this repo** — a published hook can have users this repo cannot see. That must be checked before anything is removed.

Reading 3 is the one that gates the other two, and it is not answerable from inside this repository.

⚠️ Note the interaction with PR #8521: that PR makes `columnInlineStyle` the width source for **both** Kanban layouts, so the two policies are now unambiguously one live and one dead, where before the swimlane path used neither. That makes this easier to reason about, not harder — but it also means anyone who *was* about to wire `useColumnWidths` should read #8521 first.

## Related

objectui#8508 / PR #8521 (where it was measured) · objectui#7228 — the same category one package over: `plugin-gantt`'s `columnWidthForContainer` branches on container width and returns `110` from all three arms, so its documented breakpoints do nothing. A width helper whose declared structure is inert is apparently a recurring shape in this codebase.

## Dedup

Ran, single-token `search_issues` for `useColumnWidths` — 2 hits, nearest being objectui#7228 above, which is a **different file and mechanism in the same category**, not a duplicate.

⚠️ **The result is usable; a zero from this instrument would not have been.** This repo's issue search returns false zeros — `ValueDataSource` returns `total_count: 0` while objectui#8447's own title contains that word, and recency is not the cause. A non-zero result can be read; a zero proves nothing.
